thesis_summary.thesis: Deutsche Börse Group is a leading European market infrastructure operator spanning exchanges, clearing, custody, fund distribution, indices, and buy-side software. **[Fact]** Four segments cover the transaction value chain: Investment Management Solutions (SimCorp, ISS STOXX indices and ESG data), Trading & Clearing (Eurex derivatives, Xetra cash equities, commodities, FX and digital assets), Fund Services (Clearstream fund connectivity), and Securities Services (custody, settlement, fund processing). **[Fact]** FY2025 net revenue was **€6,026 million** (+3% versus **€5,829 million** in 2024); net revenue excluding treasury result was **€5,189 million** (+9%). EBITDA was **€3,512 million** and EBITDA excluding treasury result **€2,675 million** (+14%). Net profit attributable to shareholders was **€1,995 million**; diluted earnings per share **€10.90** and cash earnings per share **€11.65** (`investor-documents/ir-db1/annual_report_2025.pdf`, Results of operations). **[Fact]** Q1 2026 net revenue excluding treasury result was **€1,434 million** (+12% versus **€1,277 million**); EBITDA excluding treasury result **€683 million** (+18%); net profit attributable to Deutsche Börse AG shareholders **€585 million** (+11%) (`investor-documents/ir-db1/quarterly_statement_q1_2026.pdf`). The company earns toll-like fees on trading, clearing, data, and fund workflows with minimal balance-sheet principal risk on core operations.
thesis_summary.why_market_wrong: No dated structural discount or yield-curve setup. **[Inference]** Q1 2026 acceleration (+12% net revenue ex treasury, +18% EBITDA ex treasury) reflects elevated volatility in rates, commodities, and equities; the market may treat that pace as durable. **[Inference]** Declining treasury result (net interest from clearing cash) masks operating strength: total net revenue grew only 9% in Q1 2026 while operating segments grew faster. We normalize on FY2025 owner cash flow, not Q1 2026 peak volumes. **Predictive attribute:** none (franchise earnings at price, not market-structure exclusion).
